name: Funding Activity
blurb:
This section is meant to track capital flowing into AI companies by funding stage and sector. In its current form it reports two aggregate counts, a running total of funding-related filings and the number of distinct companies represented, without a breakdown by month or by individual round, investor, or sector.

The totals are checked daily and the series stretches back to mid-August 2026. However, the fields meant to hold recent-round detail and month-by-month breakdowns are both currently empty in the underlying data, so this section cannot yet tell readers which companies raised money, how large specific rounds were, who invested, or how funding is trending by sector or stage. It should be read as a coarse activity counter, not a funding-news feed, until that detail is populated.

As of September 5, 2026, the tracker shows 122 funding-related filings across 47 companies, up from 119 filings on August 14, a gain of just 3 filings over three weeks. That slow, steady pace suggests the underlying filing source updates infrequently, or that filing activity itself has been quiet in this window, but the aggregate count alone cannot distinguish between those two explanations. Readers looking for specific deal terms, investor names, or round sizes will not currently find them here and should treat the two totals as a directional signal only, not a funding-news record. Filling that gap would require deal-level sourcing this section does not yet ingest, rather than a change to how the two existing totals are calculated.

reading.body:
As of September 11, 2026, 133 funding-related filings have been recorded across 52 companies, but the tracker cannot yet show which rounds closed, their size, or investor names.

The filing count has grown only 11 filings in 28 days, from 122 on August 14 to 133 on September 11. This slow movement reflects either infrequent updates from the underlying filing source or genuinely quiet funding activity during the window. The data cannot distinguish between the two. The count of distinct companies grew from 47 to 52 over the same period, suggesting some new entrants are entering the tracker even as overall filing velocity remains low.

Capital is required to build the power and compute infrastructure that AI scaling depends on. This tracker currently reports only aggregate filing counts, not the dollar amounts, stages, or sectors of any single deal. Without round-level detail, readers cannot determine whether the 133 filings represent early-stage exploration, growth-stage deployment, or infrastructure buildout. The data shows that filing activity is occurring and is rising slowly, but does not yet show whether capital is flowing toward the buildings and power systems that constrain AI development, or toward other uses.

To become actionable for tracking capital allocation in the AI infrastructure stack, this tracker would need to ingest sector tags and round sizes for each filing, and to surface month-by-month trends. Until those fields are populated, the two totals serve only as a coarse directional signal of activity level, not as a record of where money is going.
